newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs ease by noon, but investor demand strong.
newsitem.headline: JGBs ease by noon, but investor demand strong.

text.p: Cash and futures Japanese government bonds (JGBs) eased slightly by noon on Monday, but the underlying sentiment was firmly backed by persistent demand from institutional investors, traders said.
"JGBs were down on sporadic selling as early attempts to bring them up higher failed to be successful. But the mood was still bullish on investor demand," said a European bank trader.
The key September was at 125.81, down from 125.92 on Friday. It opened at 125.89 and moved in a 125.69-125.90 range.
The yield of the benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB was at 2.180 percent at 0233 GMT, up from Friday's 2.175 percent.

"Major investors, such as life and non-life insurers, have been slow to invest money earmarked for JGB investment for the April-June quarter," said Takayuki Tanaka, strategist at LTCB Securities. The JGBs have been and will be supported by buying from investors who have not yet satisfied their portfolio demand, he said.
One reason behind the bond market fall was the weaker yen, traders said. The yen fell to a low of 117.41 per dollar, down from New York's 116.82/92 on Friday.
A weaker yen, in theory, puts upward pressure on import prices and boosts inflation.
